messages:
Sam: Heads up — after yesterday's kernel-picker tweak I see a consistent ~12% p95 increase on Mixtral-8x8 for the chat endpoint. No obvious GPU saturation.
Joanna: Seen that too in canary. CPU-side tails look normal, GPU queues flash lower occupancy.
Ravi: Can you paste a perf trace? kernel names, batch distribution, and token counts would help.
Sam: Quick dump from recent run:
```
batch_sizes: [1,1,2,4,8,8,16,16]
kernel_sequence: [matmul_tiled, flash_attn_v2, kv_read, byte_fallback_tokenize, matmul_tiled]
p95: baseline=42ms, current=47ms
```
Noticed byte_fallback_tokenize appears in ~30% of requests.
Marta: Byte fallback on Mixtral is suspicious — usually Qwen hits that more with weird unicode. Any common input patterns?
Sam: App team rolled out a new system prompt template that prepends a pasted markdown blob. Some examples include non-breaking spaces and zero-width joiners. Tokenizer shows fallback tokens for those sequences.
Joanna: Ah — fallback causes a much larger token count -> larger KV writes and extra kernel invocations. Also RoPE scaling can change kernel choice if sequence length distribution shifts.
Ravi: Confirmed. When byte fallback triggers, average tokenization length jumps ~2.8x for same chars. KV cache warmup then thrashes because we end up allocating more heads segments per step.
Sam: Attaching a small sample of offending string (sanitized):
```
"System:\u00A0Please review the text\u200D\n# Notes" -> tokens: [0xA0_byte, 0x200D_byte, ...]
```
Joanna: Short-term mitigation: strip zero-width/non-breaking spaces in the prompt pipeline. Also we can force the tokenizer to use unicode-normalize NFC before tokenization.
Marta: On the runtime side we should guard kernel picker: prefer rope-aware kernels for models with RoPE scaling metadata. The recent picker change relaxed that rule which allowed a byte-optimized kernel to be chosen for Mixtral — that kernel performs worse with larger effective seq lengths.
Ravi: Agreed. Proposed patch: add a heuristic that penalizes kernels with poor kv_read performance when avg_tokens_per_request > 200 or byte_fallback_ratio > 0.1.
Sam: I ran a quick experiment forcing optimized_rope kernel and normalizing prompts: p95 went back to 43ms. Not perfect but much better.
perf-bot: perf-alert: experiment 17859: p95 reduced from 47ms -> 43ms (10k requests).
Joanna: Can we add a unit that simulates these chat templates to CI? A few synthetic sequences with invisible chars caught us here.
Marta: Yes — also add a tokenizer regression test where token_count(broken_input) < 3x token_count(normalized_input). Fail the picker if ratio > 2.5.
Ravi: For model-specific tuning: Mixtral/Mistral need kv tile sizes set to 64 for our matmul_tiled kernel. Some configs were falling back to 32 after the picker change. That increases kernel calls.
Sam: Noted. I'll push a small runtime change: restore minimum kv_tile=64 for Mixtral family and add a quick pre-tokenize normalization step in the host SDK.
Joanna: Also check BOS/EOS handling in our chat templates — double-appending EOS on streaming re-tries was observed in a couple samples, that inflates seq length and forces extra KV flushes.
Sam: Good catch. I saw two retries where both client and server added EOS. Will add de-dup on server-side.
Marta: Planed next steps: 1) deploy prompt-normalize + de-dup EOS to canary, 2) revert kernel-picker relaxation for rope models, 3) add tokenizer CI cases, 4) adjust kv_tile defaults for Mixtral.
Ravi: I'll draft the picker patch and a perf test harness for the invisible-char cases.
Sam: Thanks — will monitor canary and post numbers. If we still see >5% regression we'll roll back the picker change. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: deploy started: canary/prompt-normalize (rev b3f9)
Sam: Posting perf snapshot after deploy in ~30m.
